Multiple rounds of thunderstorms occurred from Monday April 8 through Wednesday April 10 as a deep low pressure system moved east through the Rockies, eventually transitioning to an open trough as it traversed the Plains. The first round of thunderstorms began immediately after the region experienced a total solar eclipse! Large hail was the primary severe weather occurrence on April 8th, though flooding became a primary issue on the 9th and 10th following several rounds of showers and storms.

A late spring cold front pushed south into the area on Monday June 12, and became stationary near the I-20 corridor. The front provided focus for thunderstorm development as it meandered across the region for most of that weak, with multiple upper level disturbances providing added lift for development. Several consecutive days of strong to severe storms was the result, with many areas receiving large hail (storms each day produced hail over 2) and some locations receiving damaging downburst winds between 75-95 mph. A new record hailstone for North Texas occurred on June 15th in Sanger, TX when a 5.9-inch diameter hailstone was measured.

Extreme cold gripped the county for several days. Overnight lows were near or below 20 degrees Fahrenheit almost all week. The period of February 15-16th was the coldest with low temperatures in the single digits, and the maximum temperature on the 15th was only in the mid teens. Wind chill values during the 14th-16th were between 0 to -15 degrees Fahrenheit most of the time. The cold temperatures resulted in an extreme amount of damage to pipes, infrastructure, and power. Two men are believed to have died due to poisoning from a generator. The County Medical Examiner also confirmed hypothermia to be at least a factor in the cause of death in 8 males during this period.

In Dallas County, the first round of winter weather during this period (February 13-15) resulted in snow accumulations of 2-5 inches of snow on February 14-15. The second round of winter weather (February 16-17) resulted in an additional Trace-2 inches of snow. While the winter precipitation did have an impact on the county and transportation, the bigger impacts were from the extreme cold and wind chills (see other entry). The County Medical Examiner determined hypothermia played a factor in one death on February 13th.

Areal flooding continued for several hours after scattered to numerous thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in the cities of Dallas and Irving. Up to 3.5 of rain had fallen over the city; resulting in the flooding of several streets and creeks. During the evening hours, part of the roof at the Urban Inter-Tribal Center of Texas in the Oak Cliff area collapsed under the weight of the heavy rain that had fallen earlier. As the roof collapsed, the windows in the front blew out.

Numerous high water rescues were reported around the city of Dallas as the roadways filled with water from heavy rainfall. Rainfall totals as high as 2 in 30 minutes were measured during the heavy rain event. It was also reported that the entrance to Dallas Love Field (KDAL) was closed due to high water. A 38-year old male drowned while attempting to fish in White Rock Creek near Samuell Blvd and Interstate 30 in East Dallas. The man was attempting to cross the creek, slipped, and fell into the rapidly flowing creek.

Hall Street by Baylor Hospital in Dallas was flooded due to flash flooding. One fire truck and several vehicles parked on the street stalled in this area. Water also inundated the hospital parking garage where about 20 vehicles were damaged by the rising waters. Rainfall totals as high as 2-2.25 in 30 minutes were measured during the heavy rain event.

Heavy rainfall flooded Trinity View Park and its parking lot, trapping a few visitors in the park. Several cars were flooded up to the door of the car, and three visitors had to be rescued by the Fire Department.
Multiple roads were being closed in Downtown Dallas due to flash flooding. Rainfall totals as high as 2 in 30 minutes were measured during the heavy rain event.

Northwest Highway at Hillcrest Road was closed due to high water. It was also reported that several cars were flooded out in several streets in the northeast portions of Dallas. Rainfall totals as high as 2 in 30 minutes were measured during the heavy rain event.

A surface low and an associated dryline remained over North Texas from the 29th through the early morning hours of the 31st. Several rounds of severe storms developed and moved across North Texas due to a very unstable atmosphere across the area. The main areas affected were the northern and northwestern areas of the County Warning Area. Hail up to the size of golfballs and wind gusts up to 70 MPH were reported from these storms.

The Dallas Fire Department was called to assist motorists who were stranded in high water along Camp Wisdom Road in the southwest part of the city. Camp Wisdom Rd near Chaucer Place was barricaded and parts of Kirkwood Drive were also barricaded.

An EF-0 tornado with maximum estimated winds around 85 mph occurred in Mesquite. The tornado began near Independence Drive and Meadow Lane then tracked east. Minor roof damage was noted along the track of the tornado and several large trees were split or had large branches broken off. Near the end of the track on the east side of N Galloway Ave, a car service station sustained significant damage. The winds from the tornado penetrated the building through the large service doors. The roof was ripped off the building and the back wall collapsed. The path length of this tornado was 0.3 miles with a width of about 30 yards. Two people sustained minor injuries.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported north of Seagoville.

An EF-0 tornado with maximum estimated winds around 80 mph produced damage in the city of Coppell. The tornado began near the intersection of E Belt Line Rd and S Denton Tap Rd. The awning at a gas station was damaged at this intersection. The tornado moved to the northeast through a residential area causing minor damage to some roofs of homes and businesses and also damaging trees. The total path of the tornado was 2 miles long, but the damage path was non-continuous. The damage path was also narrow at about 75 yards wide.

Two air conditioning units at the school were damaged and so was a gas line. The path length was non-continuous and was approximately 1.3 miles long with a narrow width of 30 yards.

A brief EF-0 tornado caused damage to a few trees and the roof of one home near Skyline High School in Dallas. The path of the tornado was 0.1 miles long, the width was 25 yards, and the maximum estimated winds were 80 mph.

Another round of severe weather occurred on April 26th as another upper level disturbance rounded a larger upper trough and moved into north Texas. A warm front was draped across the region, and the environment was conducive for supercell thunderstorms and tornadoes. Numerous reports of large hail and damaging winds were reported. There were 10 tornadoes confirmed on April 26th, with two rated EF-1 and the remaining rated EF-0. One EF-1 tornado occurred in Van Zandt County, near Ben Wheeler, and tracked nearly 8 miles. The winds were estimated to be near 100 MPH with this tornado. The other EF-1 tornado occurred in downtown Groesbeck causing damage to several buildings.

Hail up to the size of tennis balls and downburst winds up to 80-90 mph occurred across portions of the region. There was also 11 EF-0 tornadoes confirmed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 25th.

This tornado is a continuation from Ellis County. A tornadic supercell produced several tornado touchdowns from east of Ferris to Seagoville. The first touchdown occurred a few miles east of Ferris in open country. The tornado moved to the northeast into Dallas County where it remained in open country until it entered the city limits of Seagoville in southeast Dallas County. In Seagoville, three duplex buildings just east of HWY 175 near May Rd. suffered significant roof damage with almost complete loss of the roofs. Also, a single-family home to the northeast of the duplex buildings suffered significant roof damage. The winds estimated with this tornado at its peak intensity were…
Numerous roads and creeks remained flooded for many hours after the heavy rain had ended. Up to 8 inches of rain fell across the county.
A 65 mph wind gust was estimated at Hall Road and HWY 175 in Seagoville.

Several low water crossings in the city of Dallas were closed shortly after sunrise due to several feet of water covering the roadways. As the rain continued, additional flooding was reported. The entrance and exit ramps along Interstate 35 at Royal Lane were closed due to high water. Several high water rescues were conducted in the cities of Lancaster and Grand Prairie. A creek in Irving threatened numerous homes and 90 people were evacuated by dump trucks.
A Seagoville police officer reported quarter sized hail.
Golfball sized hail was reported at Bishop Dunne High School in Cockrell Hill.
Quarter to Golfball size hail fell in the city of Seagoville.
Power poles were bent over and 10 grain houses suffered damage in the city of Seagoville. Tree damage was also reported around the city.

Four to six inches of snow fell in the northeastern corner of the county. The public reported 4.3 of snow 1 mile east of White Rock Lake, and 4.5 of snow in Mesquite. Elsewhere in the county, an average of 0.5-2 of snow was reported. The City of Dallas police reported about 284 accidents from midnight to 10 am on the 21st. A motorcyclist was injured on North Central Expressway after skidding on an icy patch.
Nickel size hail fell in the city of Richardson.
Quarter size hail fell in the city of Irving.
Ping-pong size hail fell at the intersection of Walnut Hill and Pleasant Run in the city of Irving.

An average of 9-12 of snow fell across the county. An NWS employee measured 12.5 in Garland. Power outages and vehicles sliding off the road were numerous around the county. About 50 major accidents were reported and nearly 200 minor accidents. No serious injuries were reported. Several carports collapsed in Coppell with cars under them and several more collapsed carports were reported around the county. Just west of Dallas on Interstate 30, the roof of a tire warehouse partially collapsed around 5:30 AM on the 12th. The roof of the sanctuary at Central Pointe Church of Christ in the Red Bird area also collapsed and the sanctuary was considered a total loss.

Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. Numerous accidents were reported around the county and the DART trains were affected, too. The HOV lanes of Interstate 30 between Arlington and Mesquite were closed due to icing. The Dallas PD reported 83 accidents and 45 of these accidents resulted in injury. No further details on the injuries were provided. Road conditions improved by the afternoon. Some school districts closed for the day or delayed opening.

A police officer for the city of Richardson suffered minor injuries when his patrol car spun out of control and flipped over after hitting any icy patch. The patrol car hit a road sign and a utility pole before flipping over. A few hours later, an 18-wheeler lost control on an icy patch on East R.L. Thornton Expressway near Jim Miller Road in Dallas, causing a 5 vehicle accident. No major injuries were reported.

Snowfall totals of 1-3 of snow were reported across the county. The biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. By 645 pm, the High Five exchange was closed down. Several accidents were reported and numerous people slid off the icy roads. Some people spent the night in their cars. The Dallas County Sheriff's Office responded to 321 weather related accidents on Thursday. About 150 flights were cancelled at DFW Airport and about a handful were cancelled at Love Field.
Campbell/Blackburn Road in Garland was closed between North Garland Ave and East Brand Road due to high water.
Park Central Drive at I-635 in north Dallas was closed due to high water.
Lightning struck a home on the 900 block of Condor Drive in Coppell. The brick chimney was damaged but no other information was available.

Significant flooding continued across the southern and southwestern portions of Dallas County. Several roads remained closed. Also, the area north of Interstate 30 and south of the Trinity River in west Dallas remained flooded.

Significant flash flooding occurred across mainly the southern half of Dallas County from continuous rainfall that lasted nearly 12 hours. The Dallas EOC reported several streets southeast of downtown Dallas had to be closed. Also, the area north of Interstate 30 and south of the Trinity River in west Dallas was significantly flooded when the water pump system failed due to the heavy rainfall. Several intersections along Carrier Parkway and other major roads in Grand Prairie were flooded. Numerous other roadways in southwest Dallas County were flooded. High water rescues were performed in the southern portions of Dallas County, Interstate 45 at Simpson Stuart was closed, and the ex…
Several inches of water were flowing over Mountain Creek Parkway because ditches along the road were overflowing.
The exit ramp from Interstate 35 onto Illinois Avenue was closed due to high water. Seven cars went around the barricades and were stranded in the high water.
Three cars were trapped in high water at teh intersection of Douglas Avenue and Lemmon Avenue. The water was reported to be 9 inches deep.
Peak winds of 65 mph were reported in Richardson. Two trees were uprooted and small branches were knocked down.
Large tree limbs were down in the north Oak Cliff area.
A 67 mph wind gust was reported 1 mile south of DeSoto.
Peak winds of 60 mph were estimated in Duncanville.
The automated weather station at Grand Prairie Municipal Airport (KGPM) measured a 58 mph wind gust.
Quarter size hail fell in the city of Garland.
Quarter size hail fell in the city of Sachse.
Quarter to Golfball size hail fell in the city of Garland.
Quarter size hail fell 3 miles south of Desoto.
Half Dollar size hail fell in the city of Desoto.
Dime to Quarter size hail fell in Downtown Dallas.
Golfball size hail fell at the intersection of Skillman St. and Richmond Ave. northeast of Downtown Dallas.
Homes were evacuated near Sylvan Avenue and McBroom Street. The flooding was the result of training echoes over Dallas County.
The water was 2 feet deep at Singleton Blvd and Loop 12 on the west side of Dallas. The flooding was the result of training echoes over Dallas County.

Eight homes and one business was flooded in Mesquite. In addition, numerous roads were flooded and closed. At times, seventeen streets in the city had be closed and five of those were closed for several hours. Highway 80 at Town East Blvd had be closed and I-635 just south of Gross Road was reduced to one lane on the southbound side. A high water rescue was performed at Highway 80 and Town East Blvd at about 9:30 am. The flooding was the result of training echoes over Dallas County.
A car was stranded in 2 feet of water at Harry Hines Blvd and Northwest Highway. The flooding was the result of training echoes over Dallas County.

Significant flash flooding occurred in University Park from training echoes over Dallas County. Twenty emergency calls of vehicles stalled in water were reported to the police department and fire department. Barricades were needed in 18 locations to close down streets inundated with high water.
The water was reported to be 3 feet deep near Fair Park in Dallas. The flooding was the result of training echoes over Dallas County.
Tree branches were down on the side streets along Gaston Avenue in Dallas.
The water was reported to be 18 inches deep on the 4800 block of Gaston Ave in Dallas. The flooding was the result of training echoes over Dallas County.
Winds of 60 mph were estimated at La Vista Drive and Abrams Road.
Peak winds of 65 mph were estimated in Highland Park and a tree was blown down.
Winds of 65 mph were estimated in University Park.
Cars were stranded in high water at Elam Road and St. Augustine Road in southeast Dallas.

Two lightning strikes hit the Dallas pumping station causing the failure of one of the pumps that is responsible for parts of west Dallas. This failure exacerbated flooding that was already ongoing in Dallas. Some evacuations were performed in neighborhoods around Hampton Road and Canada Drive.

Two lightning strikes hit the Dallas pumping station causing the failure of one of the pumps that is responsible for parts of west Dallas. This failure exacerbated flooding in neighborhoods around Hampton Road and Canada Drive. Some evacuations were performed.
A lightning stike started a house fire in Mesquite. Minimal damage was sustained to the house.

Flooding was observed in North Dallas. The flooding was the result of training cells over Dallas County. The emergency manager also reported that by 7:30 am, Dallas Fire and Rescue had conducted 48 water rescues around the city and the police had worked 200 traffic accidents due to weather.

Significant flash flooding occurred in Highland Park from training echoes over Dallas County. Turtle Creek overflowed its banks and flooded roadways near its shores. A highwater rescue was required where Fitzhugh/Wycliff crosses the creek. The water was chest deep at the time of the rescue. Another water rescue was needed on Westside Drive and at the intersection of Armstrong Avenue and Lakeside Drive. Also, about 6 homes were flooded with water and the basement of the HPDPS was flooded.
Nickel size hail was reported at the intersection of I-635 and Marsh Ln in Farmers Branch.

Widespread street and creek flooding was reported around Irving. The river walk at Centennial Park in Irving was flooded, and several other parks were flooded and closed. A few motorists had to be rescued from their cars and in at least one case the water was 3-4 feet deep. Some major highways had to be closed down.
Trees were down in Hutchins.

The Lifeline Community Church on Haymarket Road in Balch Springs was damaged by high winds. Much of the roof, which was under repair at the time, was ripped off and the inside of the church was damaged. Services could not be held at the church because of the damage and it was estimated that repairs would take 3-6 months.
Peak winds of 60 mph were estimated 3 miles east of Addison. Large trees limbs were down.
KRBD (Dallas Executive Airport) ASOS measured a 71 mph wind gust.
Large tree limbs were down in Richardson.
Numerous trees were uprooted or knocked down in Coppell. Tree limbs were also knocked down. Many of the trees that were knocked over were bradford pears. Power outages also occurred.
The KDFW ASOS measured a peak wind of 64 mph.
The AWOS in Grand Prairie measured a peak wind of 58 mph.
Nickel size hail was reported in the city of Hutchins by the local Police Department.
Penny size hail was reported in Coppell.
A high water rescue was conducted at LBJ Freeway and Park Central Lane.

Heavy rain was believed to have been the cause of a roof collapse at a commercial building on the 4000 block of Sojourn Drive north of Addison Airport. The inside of the building suffered major water damage.
Numerous roads in northeast Dallas were flooded. Also, Walnut Hill Lane at Goodnight Lane was flooded.
The water was reported to be 8 inches deep across roads that run along Hickory Creek in Balch Springs.
Water was reported over the road at Interstate 20 and Highway 67.
Trees and power lines were reported down in Lancaster.
Several large trees were knocked down or split by high winds.
Several trees were snapped in half near Valwood Parkway and Crosby Road just east of Valley Ranch.

A NWS storm survey determined that a microburst with estimated 70 mph winds caused the collapse of the Dallas Cowboys' 80,000 sq ft bubble practice facility at Valley Ranch. The facility was approximately 85 feet tall and composed of a fabric shell and metal. A rookie minicamp was being held at the time and 12 people were injured. One coach was paralyzed from the waist down. Also in the area, trees were splintered and heavily damaged, but most of the damage was confined to around the practice field.

A trained spotter in Rowlett reported trees and power lines down. KDAL measured a 48 mph wind gust in association with strong winds on the back edge of the precipitation shield of the MCS. A combination of the winds and lightning knocked out power to approximately 25,000 customers.
Dime to Penny size hail was reported at Belt Line Road and Midway Road.
Nickel size hail was reported at MacArthur Blvd and Interstate 635 in Irving.
Penny size hail fell in Coppell.
Spotters reported downbursts damaged approximately 12 businesses in Dallas and Garland.
An estimated wind gust of 60 MPH was reported 3 miles southwest of Irving.

Dallas police reported at least 200 wrecks due to icy conditions, while the Rowlett police reported 11. In Farmers Branch, a driver hit a sheet of ice in a parking garage and struck a retaining wall which gave way, plunging the car about 12 feet off the second floor. The driver sustained only minor injuries. One man died after he slipped on ice, causing him to fall off a bridge almost 50 feet into the Trinity River after exiting his car following a crash. About 185 flights were canceled at DFW Airport. Spotters reported 0.5 inches of ice on trees, fences, and roofs in Richardson.
Icy tree limbs fell on power lines, causing about 48,000 residents and businesses to experience power outages across the metroplex.
Icy bridges were reported on Highway 75. A few accidents were attributed to ice, with one major accident on South Walton Walker Road in Cockrell Hill.
Dallas police responded to 173 accidents due to icy roadways, with 93 of those considered major.
A 64 MPH wind gust was measured by an ASOS at Dallas Love Field.
Service roads were closed along I-30 from previous rainfall.
Flooding was reported at Loop 12 and Stoneport Drive, the I-635 service road at South Lancaster Road, and along CF Hawn Freeway in East Dallas.
A building under construction collapsed as winds gusted near 40 MPH.
Buildings were damaged at the intersection of I-30 and Cockrell Hill.
A man died after he was struck by lightning at Lynn Creek Park on Joe Pool Lake. The man was struck in the picnic area.

Several trees fell in Park Cities and signs were blown down in the Fair Park area. At least one carport was damaged. Billboard panels near Main Street and Central Expressway was blown onto a parking lot full of cars.
A 64 MPH wind gust was measured at DFW Airport.
Flooding was reported at Oak Lawn Boulevard and North Stemmons Freeway.

A potent supercell developed during the afternoon and moved eastward along a cold front. This storm was responsible for hail as large as baseballs as it moved across Jack, Stephens, Palo Pinto, Parker, and Tarrant Counties. A squall line developed along the southward moving cold front later that evening, producing a few reports of thunderstorm winds and large hail.
A high water rescue was required at Irving Mall.
An NWS meteorologist estimated 60 MPH winds on the north side of Joe Pool Lake.
Damage occurred to several carports and a 1 foot diameter tree was blown down near Addison. In Rowlett, a few trees were downed and some roofs lost shingles.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service in Fort Worth found that a tornado touched down in DeSoto along Meadowbrook Road just west of Hampton Road. The tornado traveled east-northeast to the eastern edge of the city just north of Wintergreen Road. Several homes suffered roof damage with one home losing the majority of its roof. There were around twenty homes that sustained damage. Many downed trees, power poles, and power lines were noted along with damage to sheds and outbuildings. This tornado was rated an EF-1 with estimated maximum wind speeds of 95 MPH.
Fences, roof shingles, power lines, and trees were blown over or damaged by high winds.
Three large transmitter towers were blown down near Hebron Parkway and Eisenhower Street.

Several rounds of storms moved across north Texas on April 8th through 10th. Numerous reports of large hail were received on Tuesday evening. A lone supercell evolved during the afternoon hours of the 9th, producing tornadoes and large hail along its path. Later that evening and into Thursday morning a squall line tracked across north Texas, producing damaging winds and tornadoes into the morning hours.
A large tree was split to its base.
Penny-size hail was reported between Farmers Branch and northwest Dallas.
A high water rescue was required in north Garland after an SUV drove into high water.

Numerous streets were closed due to high water after four to six inches of rain fell across the county, including Loop 12 near White Rock Lake. Voluntary evacuations were in place for residents of DeSoto near Ten Mile Creek which overflowed its banks for the second time in less than four years. A total of sixteen roads were closed in the area. Another rescue was needed after a van stalled in high water near Lawnview Avenue and Military Parkway. There was widespread flooding in Lancaster with numerous homes flooded. Lancaster's fire department performed five high water rescues. Two teenagers were playing near a creek near Interstate 635 and Bruton Road when one of them was swept int…
DFW observing station reported a wind gust of 68 MPH.
There were numerous reports of hail and damaging winds as a cold front and upper level shortwave affected the region. The front had moved east of north Texas by late afternoon.
Golfball-size hail was reported at I-30 and Ferguson Road.
There were numerous reports of hail and damaging winds as a cold front and upper level shortwave affected the region. The front had moved east of north Texas by late afternoon.
Penny-size hail was covering the ground.
A sustained wind speed of 40 MPH was recorded in Mesquite.
A large above-ground pool was lifted and thrown against a mobile home. Windows were broken out at the home and the pool was twisted and destroyed.
A trailer overturned near Lake Ray Roberts Dam due to strong winds. The winds also caused arcing power lines which sparked several small fires.

Several vehicles were submerged near Dallas as well as a soccer field. One high water rescue was required. In Garland, ten golfers were stranded on a golf course when a creek quickly rose. They were rescued by firefighters in a raft. Interstate 635 near Mesquite had 12 inches of water over the road.
Roof damage occurred to a warehouse on the 8700 block of Diplomacy Row. Time was estimated from radar.

Several high water rescues were needed in the county. Numerous roads were closed in Dallas and Irving, including the intersections of Goodnight Road at Southwell Street, Tanner Street at X & Y Streets, Sylvan Road at Irving Road, and Interstate 35 East and Royal Lane. Northwest Highway at Loop 12 was also flooded. Citizens of northwest Irving reported torrential flooding as well.
The following intersections were barricaded due to flooding: Wynn-Joyce Road and Country Club Road and 1st Street and Avenue D. Several cars were flooded.
The east fork of the Trinity River was at least a foot out of it's banks along the Dallas/Kaufman County line.
Several streets were flooded in Lancaster, and at least one home was flooded. Interstate 35 was flooded as well.

Northwest Highway was barricaded in downtown Dallas, and a portion of Hall Road at Heard Park was closed due to flooding in Seagoville. About eight inches of water was across Central Expressway in Richardson.
Large tree limbs were blown down near Central Expressway.
Large limbs and fences were blown down.
Streets were flooded and vehicles stranded.
Minor street flooding reported.
Roads were flooded by one to two feet of water.
Several streets were flooded and closed.
Fencing, backyard furniture, and roofing was damaged as a brief tornado touched down near the recreation center. One person reported seeing a funnel cloud. One house had roof damage.
Swift water rescues were required, and a boy drowned during a rescue attempt in Duck Creek in Garland.

Water was about eight inches deep on roads in Duncanville. In Dallas, Love Freeway and South Hampton Street were closed due to flooding. Five children became stranded under a bridge in Cedar Creek and had to be rescued.
Reported on the south end of Joe Pool Lake.
Storms developed during the heat of the day along surface boundaries. Several reports of hail and one report of thunderstorm winds were received.
Trees downed.

A complex of thunderstorms moved into north Texas just after daybreak. These thunderstorms were associated with an upper level disturbance and a southward moving cold front. Several reports of wind gusts at or above 60 miles per hour were received. Storms then later redeveloped during the afternoon hours.
Service roads along Loop 12 in northwest Dallas were flooded.
Minor roof damage was reported to several buildings in town and at the Addison Airport.
One-and-a-half-feet of water over roads.
A cold front stalled across north Texas...providing focus for afternoon thunderstorms. There were several reports of hail and flash flooding.

A slow-moving upper level low pressure system resided in the Gulf coast for several days. A trough extended from this low pressure system into north Texas. Storms developed during the afternoon hours as the atmosphere destabilized. Several hail reports were received.
A 4,500 square-foot building was struck by lightning and caught fire. Damage was sustained to its roof and second floor.
Penny size hail was reported.
Large tree limbs blown down.
Measured at Dallas Executive Airport.
Large limbs blown down and power flashes reported just northwest of Addison Airport.
Numerous fences blown down, as well as roof and window damage reported in South Grand Prairie.

Numerous trees and power lines downed. Power out to about 300,000 houses and businesses in the metroplex. Plymouth House Apartments in Oak Cliff suffered major roof damage, with a large portion of the roof thrown across the road. About 60 to 70 residents were displaced. In addition to wind damage, the units also suffered water damage. In Grand Prairie, the roof of a 20,000 square foot warehouse was torn off, damaging the walls and the fuse box. An overhead sign was ripped down on Interstate 20.
Measured by a weather station owned by Lockheed Martin. Large limbs blown down.

Low level moisture was in place across North Texas as an upper level low pressure system moved into the western half of the state. Large hail reports along with damaging winds and flash flooding were common throughout this twelve-hour event.
Tree limbs broken. Estimated wind speeds of 65-70 MPH.

An area of concentrated wind damage was noted near the intersection of John West Road and Buckner Boulevard. Several trees, tree limbs, and fences were downed. Roof damage to apartments was also noted.

A strong surface low and dryline interacted with a very unstable atmosphere over North Texas. Large hail, damaging winds, and tornadoes were reported as strong storms developed. A total of 5,500 cars and 3,500 homes and businesses were reportedly damaged by hail.
Street flooding was reported in Addison.
A strong cold front and a passing upper level disturbance created an unstable atmosphere over North Texas. There were numerous hail reports and a few wind reports with this event.
A strong cold front and a passing upper level disturbance created an unstable atmosphere over North Texas. There were numerous hail reports and a few wind reports with this event.
Flash flooding reported on roads.

A high water rescue was required due to flooding at the 3500 block of East Main Street. A car was trapped under a railroad trestle. The occupant was rescued and treated for minor injuries. High water was also reported at Loop 12 and Highway 183, and on I-35 East under the Mockingbird Lane bridge.
A roof was blown off a house.

Hundreds of power lines, trees, and other structures were blown down by high winds, which were between 20 to 30 MPH sustained and gusted between 50 and 60 MPH for hours. In addition, signs and fences were blown down and shingles were blown off roofs. About 50,000 businesses and residents in the county were without power by mid-afternoon. Fires were also a problem, as the winds sparked electrical equipment and arcing power lines fell onto structures and grass. Small grassfires became large blazes due to the winds. Visibilities dropped as low as one mile at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport as a cloud of dust overspread the region. The dust cloud was clearly visible by satellit…
A half-inch of snow fell across the county.

Between one and three-inches of snow fell across the metroplex. About a quarter of the flights departing from the Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport were cancelled due to the weather. Dallas County reported around 115 wrecks due to the slick driving conditions.

Several roads were closed due to icing during this event, including U.S. Highway 67 in Cedar Hill, and Spur 408 at Intersate 20. Large limbs were downed due to the icing in Duncanville. Hundreds of accidents were reported with cars sliding off roads and into one another. One woman died when her car slid into a tractor-trailer on Interstate 30. About 400 flights were cancelled from Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport. Around 2,500 people in the county were without power as power lines were downed by falling branches and trees laden with ice.

A mixture of freezing rain, snow, and sleet fell across the metroplex, causing 2,700 power outages across the area. Hundreds of accidents were reported as well, with several hundred flights cancelled at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport.

Power was knocked out to at least 17,000 households Wednesday morning in the Dallas/Fort Worth area as sustained strong winds knocked over power poles and transformers. Large trees and limbs were knocked down throughout the county. Fences, signs, trampolines, and other outdoor items were blown around as well. Additionally, 160 flight were cancelled at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport.
The Irving police department reported high water along Highway 183, Loop 12 at Highway 114, and side streets.
Lightning struck near a residential pool on the 400 block of Chelsea Bay. Firefighters found smoking breakers and the pool equipment inoperable.

Four mobile homes and two homes under construction were damaged one mile west of Seagonville. In addition, trees were uprooted and power lines downed throughout the county. Damage was reported along the North Central Expressway in northeast Dallas; in an area encompassed by Interstate 35 East to the north, Loop 12 to the west, and Interstate 30 to the south. Similar damage was also reported in the southern part of the county. Power was knocked out to about 4,500 customers.

Lightning struck a house on the 300 block of Still Forest. The lightning destroyed all the wiring in the house, also damaging the roof, insulation, sheetrock, and carpet. The Fire Marshall estimated damages at $60,000.
Lightning struck a home causing a fire to erupt at the residence. The extent of the damage was not known. There were no injuries.
At least one power line was blown down. The former Dallas City Manager was electrocuted and killed while investigating the downed power line.
A 60 MPH wind gust was measured on the northern side of Lancaster. A hotel awning was torn off and trees and power lines were blown down in Hutchins.
61 MPH wind gust reported at the Lockheed Martin building located in the west part of town.
Trees down on Johnson Lane along the Dallas/Ellis County line.
Relayed by Lake Charles National Weather Service Forecast Office.
Official observation at Dallas/Fort Worth Airport of 60 MPH wind gust.

A fast moving cold front brought strong northwest winds and blowing dust to north Texas Friday afternoon. Visibilities dropped to 3 miles in some locations due to the blowing dust. Measured wind gusts reached 51 MPH at Meacham Airport in Fort Worth and at Addison Airport in north Dallas. Several thousand people lost power. Minor damage was reported around the area, with several windows blown out of downtown Dallas skyscrapers. Downed trees and power lines were also reported.
Heavy rain collapsed the roof and walls of a gun range near Love Field.

Heavy rains caused many road closures, high water rescues, and evacuations of homes and businesses throughout the afternoon and evening. Water was reportedly five feet high in some homes, causing significant damage. Water rose four feet high in the lower level of the Renaissance Hotel on Stemmons Freeway near Wycliff Avenue. Dallas police received more than 240 calls about people in danger from the flood waters in four hours. A woman was swept away in Turtle Creek by Wycliff Avenue after she abandoned her car due to rapidly rising flood waters. Her body was recovered later that night nearly a mile from were she was swept away.
Water was flowing over Northwest Highway from Whiterock Creek in Dallas County. Also, Cedar Creek Lake in Henderson County was reported out of its banks and flooding nearby streets in Payne Springs.

Light precipitation fell as temperatures hovered around freezing for much of the weekend. Dozens of accidents related to the icy conditions were reported in several counties. There were numerous injuries and at least 5 fatalities indirectly related to the winter weather. The Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport cancelled approximately 100 flights on Saturday alone.

A winter storm dropped a quarter-inch of ice on the Dallas/Fort metroplex. Hundreds of accidents were reported throughout the event across the county. The Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport cancelled 500 flights on Wednesday as the planes were unable to depart.
Widespread wind damage occurred, including trees and power lines down.
Large tree limbs down and power poles snapped.
Reported by ASOS.
A tree was blown onto a car in an apartment complex.
Several cars were stranded in two-foot deep water. Three inches of rain fell in 45 minutes.
Three inch tree limbs broken off.
Trees and power lines blown down over roadway.
Large tree blown down on top of home, causing considerable damage to a house in the Oak Cliff area.
5 inch tree limbs broken off causing widespread power outages.
Street flooding reported in SE Dallas and Mesquite.
Minor street flooding up to car bumpers at Big Town Boulevard and Highway 80.
Tornado touched down briefly. No damage reported.
Ping pong ball size hail covering ground.
Hail the size of hen eggs reported.
Spotter reported quarter size hail at Bruton Road and 175.
I-45 exit closed due to high water.
Exit ramp in town is flooded.
Flooding closed Brand and Campbell Roads in Garland.

A mixture of snow and sleet spread across North Central Texas during the early morning and daytime hours, affecting virtually all of North Central Texas. Snow and sleet accumulations ranged from a trace in the southeast up to 3 inches in Eastland and Erath counties. The biggest problem was delays in airline flights in the DFW area, and reports of over 500 traffic accidents due to ice and snow packed roads, bridges, and overpasses.

A severe thunderstorm produced damage from the east side of Grand Prairie, north northeast across eastern Irving and into west Dallas. At 105 pm Dallas Love Field had measured wind gusts to 76 mph,with estimates as high as near 100 mph across Grand Prairie and Irving. Three tractor-trailer rigs were blown over on Interstate 30, and parts of Loop 12 near Texas Stadium were closed for a while because of downed powerlines across the lanes. Several businesses in Grand Prairie sustained structural damage.A motel on the Stemmons Freeway in Dallas had 12 units unroofed, and one new automobile dealership had over 100,000 dollars damage.

Many roads and highways were flooded and closed, and homes were evacuated, especially in south Dallas where over 13 inches of rain fell in 12 hours. There were over 80 high water rescues in the county.

175-200 homes were flooded, numerous streets were completely flooded, people were stranded in cars, andnumerous high water rescues were needed. The police station was also flooded. Lancaster recieved over 7 inches of rain in 12 hours.
There were numerous reports of power lines down across the city.
Occurred in downtown Dallas.
Streets in town were flooded.
Occurred between Balch Springs and Seagoville.
Occurred between Balch Springs and Seagoville.
Three inch diameter tree limbs down at the intersection of Saturn and Northwest Highway.
One foot diameter trees blown down near the Addison Airport.
Roads were closed in Northwest and Northeast Dallas, and water was over a road 2 miles northwest of Irving due to high water.
Large steel framed building blown down by high winds.
Quarter size hail fell near White Rock Lake.
Over 1,000 city trees were blown down by high winds.
High winds blew out some windows in the terminal building.
Occurred 5 miles north of downtown Dallas.
Trees were blown down between Seagoville and Rowlett.

An upper level storm system moved across North Central Texas late Friday night February 13th, and during the day Saturday February 14th, producing measurable snow across all but extreme southeast parts of North Texas. Snow began falling Friday night across the southwest parts of North Texas, then spread northeast across the rest of the region late Friday night and early Saturday morning. The snow ended over southwest parts of the region Saturday morning, and across the northeast early Saturday evening. Heavy snow of 4 to 5.5 inches fell on the 14th, from Montague and Wise counties eastward as far as Lamar and Delta counties, and south into northern Tarrant, northern Dallas, and nor…
Interstate 635 closed at Interstate 75 due to flooding in North Dallas.
Trees were blown down by high winds.
A man was killed as he sought refuge behind the wall of a Home Depot under construction. High winds blew the wall down on him. The time is estimated.
Trees were blown down by high winds.
The Westridge Apartments suffered wind damage. One unit destroyed, five had major damage, andthree had minor damage.
Trees were damaged by high winds.
High winds broke windows and damaged a wall.
Power lines were blown down on the south side of Plano near the Richardson city limits.
A home and business was flooded, and a roof partially collapsed from water.
20 apartment units were unroofed and flooded in Pleasant Grove. There were also numerous reports of trees and power lines blown down.
Occurred on the east side of White Rock Lake.
Numerous large tree limbs, 6-8 inches in diameter blown down.
Occurred at Loop 12 and Interstate 30 on the west side of Dallas.
Occurred at Joe Pool Lake.

Thunderstorms developed along a cold front just northwest of the Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area and spread southeast during the late afternoon and evening hours. Most of the severe weather was large hail; up to softball size in Hood county. The storms did produce some wind damage across south central and southeast parts of North Texas.

At 1948 CDT, a large, slow moving high precipitation supercell began moving into western Dallas County. A squall line merged with this storm producing record rainfall across Dallas. In some areas over three inches of rain fell in 30 minutes and five inches in one hour. Massive flash flooding occurred, with areas flooding that have never flooded before. Sixteen people drowned and many people were stranded and had to be rescued.
